page: Amazon Web Services i8g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and a bundled local storage capacity of 15000 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 38 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core and memory-bound operations. The server achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks, alongside top-tier outcomes in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the average tier.

The instance demonstrates a distinct performance profile for large language model inference, where text generation for a medium 7B model reaches top-tier speeds, whereas text generation for a small 135M model falls into the weak tier. This resource density makes the server qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out database workloads, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive data processing. It is highly suited for database deployments, Redis caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
